recentItems.title: National Archives Museum Rotunda Drone Flight
recentItems.description:
Get up close with the U.S. Constitution at the National Archives Museum- and see it like never before! This week marks the beginning of #ConstitutionWeek, and as we prepare for #ConstitutionDay on September 17, take a flight with us inside the historic Rotunda! Get tickets to see it now, including the special temporary display of George Washington's Annotated Copy of a Draft of the U.S. Constitution, on display through September 27.

Make plans to see the Rotunda and all of our exhibits at visit.archives.gov/visit/tickets!

And for the record, this video is NOT AI.

recentItems.title: United States Coast Guard Founding-Era Records #OpeningTheVault
recentItems.description:
Are you curious how the U.S. Coast Guard became the military branch we know today? 

On August 4, 1790, Congress created the Revenue-Cutter Service to enforce tariff and trade laws, prevent smuggling, and protect the collection of federal revenue.

In 1878, the U.S. Life-Saving Service began rescuing shipwreck survivors and by 1915, these two services merged, officially forming the Coast Guard.

Dive into history with us as we uncover the public laws that shaped the Coast Guard, straight from the National Archives vault.

recentItems.title: National Archives Fulbright Scholar Researches Paper-Based Preservation
recentItems.description:
Yu Lin is researching an often overlooked challenge in preservation: the long-term effects of correction materials like fluids and tapes on paper-based archives.

Hosting Fulbright scholars through our U.S. Department of State partnership is vital to our mission to ensure high-quality preservation standards are applied to our holdings. Research partnerships help us anticipate future preservation risks and provide evidence-based guidance for the archivists and conservators who care for our records globally.

recentItems.title: PIDB Open Meeting on Capitol Hill 7/15/26
recentItems.description:
The statutorily bipartisan Public Interest Declassification Board hosts an Open Meeting focused on how it serves Congress as a productive partner on classification and declassification issues. The Board also details what it sees as the critical components for legislation prompting successful declassification and public release of records.

Guest participants include: The Honorable Representative Eric Burlison (R-MO), the Honorable Representative Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), the Honorable Representative Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL), and John Powers, Acting Director, Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State.

For more information, visit the PIDB website: https://www.archives.gov/declassification/pidb, check out the PIDB blog: https://transforming-classification.blogs.archives.gov/, and follow the PIDB on X: https://x.com/PublicDeclass

recentItems.title: How the National Archives Protects the Declaration of Independence
recentItems.description:
Have you ever wondered what it takes to protect the Declaration of Independence?

Go behind the scenes as we reveal how the Charters Monitoring System allows the National Archives Conservation Branch to detect and measure the founding document’s conditions.

Today, the Declaration of Independence rests in a state-of-the-art, titanium encasement designed to last 100 years. We’re 23 years in, and the Declaration remains unchanged and ready to be viewed as we celebrate #America250.
